facts.statement: The species Gobihadros mongoliensis was formally named and described in 2019 by Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, David Bruce Weishampel, David Christopher Evans, and Mahito Watabe.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Gobihadros mongoliensis was named and described by Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, David Bruce Weishampel, David Christopher Evans, and Mahito Watabe.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPC-D100/746 was discovered in the Bayan Shireh Formation from the Cenomanian-Santonian stages.
facts.quote: The holotype, MPC-D100/746, was found in a layer of the Bayan Shireh Formation dating from the Cenomanian-Santonian stages.

facts.statement: Gobihadros is classified as a medium-sized hadrosauroid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Gobihadros was a medium sized hadrosauroid.

facts.statement: Gobihadros is distinguished from other non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroids by having a double-layered tomial edge on the premaxilla and up to three teeth per position in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Gobihadros differs from all known other non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroids in possessing a double-layered tomial edge of the premaxilla and the presence of as much as three teeth per tooth position in the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Gobihadros possesses a conical, spike-like claw on its first finger, a trait not found in Tethyshadros, Plesiohadros, or Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Gobihadros differs from T. insularis, Plesiohadros djadokhtaensis and the Hadrosauridae in possessing a conical spike-like claw of the first finger.

facts.statement: The largest known fully grown individual of Gobihadros reached an estimated length of 7.5 meters.
facts.quote: It contains only the type species Gobihadros mongoliensis, which has an estimated length of 7.5 m.

facts.statement: Gobihadros lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 100,5 y 83,6 millones de años, desde el Cenomaniense al Santoniense

facts.statement: Fossils of Gobihadros have been found in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Gobihadros is classified within the superfamily Hadrosauroidea in a basal position outside the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Gobihadros was placed in the Hadrosauroidea in 2019, in a basal position outside of the Hadrosauridae.

facts.statement: CT scans of a large Gobihadros individual revealed calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease in its tail vertebrae and foot bones.
facts.quote: These paleopathologies were interpreted to represent traces of calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease, and were found in caudal vertebrae and pedal phalanges.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease found in this dinosaur likely resulted from old age rather than physical trauma.
facts.quote: It is likely that the disease developed in the dinosaur due to old age rather than external factors, such as physical trauma.

facts.statement: Life Science Identifiers were required to validate the name Gobihadros because the description was published in an electronic journal.
facts.quote: Because the describing article appeared in an electronic publication, Life Science Identifiers were needed to make the name valid.

rejected.statement: The combined fossil material makes Gobihadros the most completely known basal hadrosauroid from Asia.
rejected.quote: Combined, they make Gobihadros the most completely known basal hadrosauroid from Asia.
